Explain it.","marks":0,"answer":"The exponent of the fundamental quantities present in a physical quantity is called the dimension of that quantity.
For example: Force = mass × acceleration
\[ = \text{mass} \times \frac{\text{velocity}}{\text{time}} \]
\[ = \text{mass} \times \frac{\text{displacement}}{(\text{time})^2} \]
Here, dimension of displacement is L, dimension of mass M and dimension of time is T. Now putting them into this force equation, we get \(\frac{\text{ML}}{T^2}\) or, MLT\(^{-2}\). That it the dimension of force MLT\(^{-2}\) means force is a derived quantity.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Determine how many division of vernier scale of a slide caliper is equal to the how many division of the main scale.","marks":0,"answer":"We know,
\[ \text{vernier constant} = \frac{\text{Magnitude of 1 smallest division of main scale (s)}}{\text{Total number of divisions of vernier scale (n)}} \]
or, \( VC = \frac{s}{n} \)
\[ s = 1 \, \text{mm} \]
or, \( n = \frac{s}{VC} = \frac{1}{0.05} = 20 \)
\[ VC = 0.005 \, \text{cm} = 0.05 \, \text{mm} \]
Again, We know
vernier constant (\( VC \)) = Magnitude of 1 smallest division of main scale (s) – Magnitude of 1 smallest division of vernier scale.
Magnitude of 1 smallest division of vernier scale
\[ = s - VC = 1 - 0.05 = 0.95 \, \text{mm} \]
Then, magnitude of 20 smallest division of vernier scale
\[ = 20 \times 0.95 = 19 \, \text{mm} = 19 \times s = 19 \times \text{Magnitude of 1 smallest division of main scale} \]
That it, vernier scale's 20 parts is equals to main scales 19 parts. (Ans.)

Inner length of hollow iron box,
\[ l_2 = M_2 + V_2 \times VC \]

\[ = 6.03 \, \text{cm} \]

\[ V.C. = 0.005 \, \text{cm} \]

\[ = (8.045)^3 - (6.03)^3 \]

[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What is least count of a screw gauge?","marks":0,"answer":"If the circular scale is rotated only one division the distance that the screw covers for that one rotation is said to be least count of the screw gauge.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Write down two differences between fundamental and derived quantities.","marks":0,"answer":"Two differences between fundamental and derived quantities are given below:
| Fundamental Quantity | Derived Quantity |
|---|---|
| 1. The quantities that require no other quantities to express themselves are called fundamental quantities. | 1. The quantities that are expressed using one or more fundamental quantities are called derived quantities. |

","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"If the relative error in measuring the length of the cubic stone is 10%, determine the relative error in its volume in the light of scenario-1.","marks":0,"answer":"Measured volume of the cube = \(8^3 \, \text{cm}^3\) = 512 cm\(^3\)
If there is 10% relative error in measuring the length of one side then,
Probable smallest length = \((8 - 8 \times 10\%)\) cm = 7.2 cm
∴ Probable smallest volume = \((7.2)^3 \, \text{cm}^3\) = 373.25 cm\(^3\)
∴ Error in volume = \((512 - 373.25) \, \text{cm}^3\) = 138.75 cm\(^3\)
Again, Probable largest length = \((8 + 8 \times 10\%)\) cm = 8.8 cm
∴ Probable largest volume = \((8.8)^3 \, \text{cm}^3\) = 681.472 cm\(^3\)
∴ Error in volume = \((681.472 - 512) \, \text{cm}^3\) = 169.472 cm\(^3\)
As the error is greater in the second case, taking 169.472 cm\(^3\) as error we get,
\[ \frac{169.472}{512} \times 100\% = 33.1\% \text{ (Ans.)} \]
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"The measurement in length of the piece of wood by the help of slide calipers is more accurate and acceptable than ordinary scale–Analyze mathematically in the light of scenario-2.","marks":0,"answer":"Here we see, the main scale reading of the wood is 13.5 cm.

\[ VC = \frac{\text{Length of the 1 smallest division of the main scale}}{\text{Number of divisions in the vernier scale}} \]
\[ \Rightarrow VC = \frac{1 \, \text{mm}}{10} = 0.1 \, \text{mm} = 0.01 \, \text{cm} \]
Length of the wood, L = M + V × VC
\[ = 13.5 + 4 \times 0.01 \]
\[ = 13.54 \, \text{cm} \]
Therefore, with the help of slide calipers, the measurement of the wood can be done more accurately than with the ordinary scale.

[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What is called the pitch of a screwgauge?","marks":0,"answer":"The pitch of the screw gauge is the distance moved by the spindle for one rotation.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Verify the accuracy of the equation \( s = ut + \frac{1}{2} at^2 \)","marks":0,"answer":"We can verify any equation by its dimensional equation.
We know,
dimension of displacement = L
dimension of time = T
dimension of velocity = LT\(^{-1}\)
dimension of acceleration = LT\(^{-2}\)
for the equation of \( s = ut + \frac{1}{2} at^2 \)
L.H.S. = \( s = \text{displacement} = L \)
R.H.S = \( ut + \frac{1}{2} at^2 \)
\[ = \text{velocity} \times \text{time} + \frac{1}{2} \times \text{acceleration} \times \text{time}^2 \]
\[ = LT^{-1} \times T + \frac{1}{2} \times LT^{-2} \times T^2 \]
\[ = L + \frac{1}{2} L \]
\[ = L + L \text{ (ignoring the constant)} \]
\[ = L \]
∴ L.H.S. = R.H.S.
That is, \( s = ut + \frac{1}{2} at^2 \) equation is verified.

Real area of the square object,
\[ A = a^2 = (1.875)^2 = 3.5156 \, \text{cm}^2 \]

\[ A_{\text{max}} = (1.875 + 0.09375)^2 = 3.876 \, \text{cm}^2 \]
The minimum area of square object,

Final error for the maximum area
\[ \Delta A = |A_{\text{max}} - A| = |3.876 - 3.5156| = 0.3604 \, \text{cm}^2 \]

\[ \Delta A = 0.3604 \, \text{cm}^2 \]
∴ The relative error in measurement of area
\[ = \frac{\Delta A}{A} = \frac{0.3604}{3.5156} = 0.1025 = 10.25\% \]
To determining the area of square object, 10.25% of error will occur.
